blocking.section: Control plane and data plane version skew (skew table, regional relay row; Ruralz Control upgrades rules 3 and 4; Figure 2)
blocking.issue: The relay row puts a relay one minor behind the replicas inside policy after finalize. It also says relays upgrade 'after the replicas', which can fall after finalize, since Nodes upgrade only after finalize. But the relay is subject to the 'Same halt rule', and the relay feed streams committed entries on 8092. After finalize that includes the version-advance entry and N record types or migrations, which rule 3 applies only then. An N-1 relay that follows the in-policy path therefore meets a Control Store version above its binary's and stops (rule 4), or receives N encodings it is not required to decode. Every Node that dials that relay loses Rollouts until the relay is upgraded. The finalize gate and Figure 2 count only replicas, so nothing stops an operator from reaching this state.
blocking.evidence: Line 144: "| Regional Ruralz Control relay, Planned (M4) | The replicas' minor or one older; upgrades after the replicas, before its Nodes | Two minors older; newer than the replicas | Same halt rule; form: OQ-system-overview-16 |". Line 172: "Migrations, new record types and N defaults apply only after it". Line 173: "A replica meeting a Control Store version above its binary's, or an unknown entry type, stops before serving". Figure 2: "g{"Every replica, voters and non-voters, reports N?"}". Control plane and GitOps, Relay feed: "It streams committed entries filtered to the relay's Clusters: plan and assignment state with `storeEpoch` and `assignmentSeq`, signed promotions, revocations, anchor sets and `clusterNodeCount`."
blocking.fix: Change the relay row to: In policy "N-1 and N while the Control Store version is N-1; N after finalize; upgrades after every replica reports N and before finalize"; Outside policy "N-2; N-1 after finalize; newer than the replicas". Extend rule 1 and rule 3 to relays: "Each replica, voter or non-voter, and each relay reports its binary version ..." and "Once every replica and relay reports N ...". Relabel Figure 2 node g to "Every replica, voters and non-voters, and every relay reports N?" and add a node before g: "Upgrade relays to N". The alternative is to state that the relay feed keeps N-1 encodings and entry types until the next finalize. If the writer takes that route, the row must say so and the rule 4 halt must not apply to relays at N-1.

blocking.section: Control plane and data plane version skew (Ruralz Control upgrades rules 3 and 4, Upgrade order, Figure 2 node p)
blocking.issue: The one-minor-at-a-time rule is enforced only from one side. Rule 4 halts a binary that is older than the Control Store version, but nothing halts a binary that is too new. Two cases are unprotected. The first is an operator skipping a minor, such as N+1 binaries on a Control Store at N-1, a common mistake with image tags. The second is starting N+1 before every replica has reported its post-finalize snapshot, which rule 3 forbids. In both, the new binary starts and decodes snapshots and log entries older than its N-1 decode guarantee. Rule 3 says the leader 'refuses the next upgrade', but it does not say how: upgrading is an operator replacing a binary, and no refusal path, error code or halt is defined. Figure 2 node p has no 'no' branch. An operator therefore cannot tell what happens, or what they will see, when the precondition is unmet.
blocking.evidence: Line 172: "Every replica then forces a snapshot past that index, truncates its log and reports to the leader, which refuses the next upgrade until all have." Line 173: "A replica meeting a Control Store version above its binary's, or an unknown entry type, stops before serving". Line 171: "N binaries MUST decode every N-1 entry, record and snapshot." Line 184: "Ruralz Control moves one minor at a time (rule 3)". Figure 2: "p -- \"yes\" --> a" (no 'no' edge).
blocking.fix: Extend rule 4: "A replica whose binary minor is more than one above the Control Store version, or whose local snapshot predates the last version-advance entry, stops before serving and exports a metric. The leader rejects status reports from a binary newer than the Control Store version until every replica has reported its post-finalize snapshot, using an `RZ-CP` code that Control plane and GitOps registers. That is how it refuses the next upgrade." In Upgrade order add: "Skipping a minor is refused: upgrade through each minor in turn." In Figure 2 add the edge p -- no --> a wait node: "Wait: an N+1 replica would be refused and stop".
